FINDING 5 — `main`'s return type is unchecked, and a non-i32 `main` yields a
GARBAGE process exit status from the C backend (and a different one from JS).

FILE: main_void_exit_status_garbage.zen.txt
CMD:  ./zen run tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/main_void_exit_status_garbage.zen.txt ; echo rc=$?
OUT:  42
      rc=3                    <-- 3 == the byte count of "42\n"
CMD:  ./zen build <file> -o /tmp/m.bin && /tmp/m.bin ; echo rc=$?
OUT:  42
      rc=3                    <-- same for a built binary, not a `run` artifact
CMD:  ./zen emit-js <file> | node ; echo rc=$?
OUT:  42
      rc=0                    <-- the JS backend exits 0

CAUSE: genc emits `void zen_main()` for a `() void` main, but the runtime calls
      it as an int: bootstrap/zenrt.c:40  `ZWEAK int32_t zen_main(void)` and
      :223 `return (int)zen_main();`. The strong symbol overrides the weak
      prototype, so `main` returns whatever the return register happens to
      hold — here the result of the last `write()` inside println (println now
      returns the byte count, commit 34755b8).

OTHER RETURN TYPES (all accepted by the checker, all garbage):
      main = () void        -> rc 3    (bytes printed)
      main = () bool        -> rc 1
      main = () f64         -> rc 3    (double is not in the int return reg)
      main = () StringView -> rc 199  (low byte of a pointer)
      main = () i32         -> correct

NOT COVERED ANYWHERE: `grep -c 'main = () void'` over examples/ and
      tests/fixtures/zen/ is 0; all 248 fixtures use `main = () i32`. This
      shape has no test at all.
CLASS: C/JS divergence in exit status + undefined behaviour in the C floor +
      missing checker rule on main's signature.
FOUND BY: hand-directed probing of i32/i64 boundary arithmetic (the exit code
      of the probe program was the first thing that looked wrong).
